name: EPA NPDES sewer overflow and bypass event reports (eRule Phase 2, "SOBE"), Illinois permits
operator: U.S. EPA (ECHO), data entered by Illinois permittees in NeT-SewerOverflow
waters_covered: statewide; every Illinois NPDES permittee that files through EPA NeT-SewerOverflow
access_detail: Daily ZIP (1.1 MB on 2026-11-03, Last-Modified 2026-11-03 12:13 GMT) of CSV tables: sewer_overflow_bypass_report_events.csv joined on sewer_overflow_bypass_event_key to _types, _receiving_waters, _causes, _impacts, _corrective_actions; collection_system_permits.csv names the system. Filtered on permit_identifier LIKE IL%. Summary of IL rows in raw/sobe-permit-counts.json, raw/sobe-by-seed-permit.json, raw/sobe-top-noncso-permits.json; newest row in raw/sobe-latest-sample.json.
cadence: EPA refreshes daily. Illinois rows: 1,687 events from 267 permits; report received a median 3 days after the start (90th percentile 11 days). Newest row on 2026-11-03: an SSO that started 2026-11-02 12:00 and was received 2026-11-02.
license: EPA public data; no licence restriction stated on the ECHO download page.
legal_basis: 40 CFR 122.41(l)(6) and (l)(7); 40 CFR part 127 (eRule Phase 2, from 2025-12-21)
status_reason: The only statewide, machine-readable, event-level overflow table for Illinois. Every row has coordinates; 95% have a volume. Types: SSO 1,256, CSO 341, BYP 90. It misses the big Cook County CSO systems: no CSO-typed rows from Chicago (IL0045012), MWRD Stickney/O'Brien/Calumet, or the 37 ILM580xxx suburban CSO general permits. Only 17 of the 120 CSO permits have a CSO-typed row.
notes: Pekin STP #1 (IL0034495) alone has 115 CSO rows. Times carry no time zone (assume America/Chicago; see federal report). Receiving-water names are free text ("marys river maybe").

name: MWRD CSO Event Synopsis Report (per-outfall tide-gate open and close times by event day)
operator: Metropolitan Water Reclamation District of Greater Chicago
waters_covered: Chicago Area Waterway System: North Shore Channel, North and South Branch Chicago River, Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal, Des Plaines River, Little Calumet and Calumet-Sag; MWRD-monitored outfalls of Chicago, MWRD and suburban owners
access_detail: ASP.NET page with a drop-down of event dates (ddlCSODates; 364 dates from 4/1/2016 to 10/15/2026). A POST with the page's hidden fields, the date and __EVENTTARGET=bttSearchDay, in the same cookie session, renders an SSRS ReportViewer. Its ExportUrlBase plus Format=CSV returns a CSV (raw/mwrd-csoreport-20261015.csv, raw/mwrd-csoreport-20260704.csv). The script is in research notes only; no key needed.

sample_record.location: Wilson Ave ext. (Wilson & East River Rd) (E)
sample_record.rain: Central Basin 0.4 Low; North Basin 0.6 Moderate; South Basin 0.5 Moderate

cannot_fill: coordinates (join TARP_CONNECTION to the CSO_Points layer)
cadence: Dates appear after MWRD staff compile them; 10/15/2026 was the newest on 2026-11-03 (no event days since by MWRD's list). Exact posting latency not measured: poll daily for a week.
history: Event dates back to 4/1/2016 in this app; an older app (apps.mwrd.org/CSO/CSOEventSynopsisSelectD.aspx) holds 2014 to 5/14/2016.
license: No terms stated on the page.
legal_basis: NPDES permits IL0028053, IL0028088, IL0028061 CSO special conditions; 40 CFR 122.38
status_reason: Per-outfall open and close times for Cook County since 2016, but reached only through a form, a session and a report viewer: by the standing rule on bot walls and polling forms it is not read by an automated session; the request to MWRD is a download or feed of the same table (register row il-mwrd-cso-synopsis-report).
notes: 7/4/2026 report has 24 outfall rows. The monitored set includes City of Chicago and suburban outfalls tied to TARP drop shafts.

name: MWRD "Possible CSO Events" live map layer
operator: Metropolitan Water Reclamation District of Greater Chicago
waters_covered: Chicago Area Waterway System and Lake Michigan reversal points
access_detail: Public MapServer layer, no token. query?where=1=1&outFields=*&f=json returned count 0 on 2026-11-03 (no event in progress). Service description: "This is the master CSO layer. Updates to CSO_EVENT are copied to an Archive layer nightly and the layer's fields are reset." App: https://mwrdgc.maps.arcgis.com/apps/instant/sidebar/index.html?appid=1a2bc307bc404d9e927528fd215da022 (raw/mwrd-possible-cso-app.json).
cadence: The app says "updated daily and reflects unconfirmed CSO and diversion activity"; reset nightly.
history: None (current state only; the Archive layer is not public).
status_reason: Read hourly by pipeline/ingest/il_mwrd_possible_cso.py: each outfall on the map becomes an unconfirmed CSO record for that day (start the layer's edit time, no end invented); empty when no activity is shown.
notes: App disclaimer quoted: "Not all CSO outfalls are equipped with monitoring equipment. Therefore, other CSOs may have occurred that are not reflected on the above map. Regardless of CSO activity, the Chicago Area Waterways may contain disease-causing bacteria at any time. Therefore, swimming, canoeing, or other activities where immersion in water is possible should be avoided and is not recommended, particularly during and immediately following rainfall."

name: MWRD CSO Points (outfall layer, Cook County)
operator: Metropolitan Water Reclamation District of Greater Chicago
access_detail: Public FeatureServer; 441 points; dataLastEditDate 2026-06-29. Sample in raw/mwrd-cso-points-sample.json.
status_reason: Better than the EPA inventory for Cook County: 441 outfalls from 51 owners (Chicago 214, MWRD 51, Evanston 16, Maywood 13), 273 monitored and 168 unmonitored, with the TARP drop-shaft key that joins the synopsis report.
notes: No NPDES outfall number; match to EPA inventory by location.

name: MWRD CSO notification alerts (email and SMS, via Smart911)
operator: Metropolitan Water Reclamation District of Greater Chicago
access_detail: Sign-up https://www.smart911.com/smart911/ref/reg.action?pa=mwrdcso (account on a third-party platform). Page: "CSO notifications are available via both email and SMS/text." "provides notification of CSO events and waterway diversions to Lake Michigan within the MWRD service area." Moved to the new system 2025-06-17; old subscribers had to re-register (Friends of the Chicago River).
cadence: Event-driven; intended to meet the 4-hour rule of 40 CFR 122.38.
legal_basis: 40 CFR 122.38(a)(3); NPDES permit public notification special conditions
status_reason: The legally required public channel, but email/SMS behind a Smart911 account; owner sign-up only. WTTW (2025): alerts say only that an overflow occurred somewhere in the MWRD network.

name: 40 CFR 122.38 Great Lakes Basin CSO public notification (applies to the Chicago-area CSO permits)
access_detail: eCFR XML fetched (raw/ecfr-122-38.xml).
status_reason: EPA's Great Lakes CSO page for Illinois lists 42 NPDES CSO permits, "All 42 of these NPDES CSO permits are in the Chicago metropolitan area" (Chicago, MWRD x4, and the TARP suburbs). Downstate CSOs (Peoria, Pekin, Galesburg ...) drain to the Mississippi and are not covered.
notes: (a)(3)(i): "As soon as possible, but no later than four (4) hours after becoming aware by monitoring, modeling or other means that a CSO discharge has occurred, the Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee shall provide public notification of CSO discharges ... electronically, such as by text, email, social media alerts to subscribers or by posting a notice on its public access website".

name: Illinois EPA sanitary sewer overflow notification form and regional-office 24-hour rule
access_detail: Search snippet only: "Within 24 hours of the occurrence, notify the Illinois EPA regional wastewater staff by telephone, FAX, email or voice mail" and "Failure to notify may result in fines up to $10,000 for each day of violation." Permit standard condition mirrors 40 CFR 122.41(l)(6).
legal_basis: NPDES permit standard conditions; 415 ILCS 5/12; 35 Ill. Adm. Code 309
status_reason: Regulator-only report; no Illinois statute or rule requiring public notice of an SSO was found.
